Operator: Good day, and welcome to the Nexus Telecom Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. There will be an opportunity to ask a question after the presentation. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Nexus Telecom's Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Chen, Chief Executive Officer; Mike Patel, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Sarah Chen: Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for Q2 2024. We achieved solid revenue growth and expanded margins, which reflects our strong execution in a dynamic market. We are particularly excited about the initial performance of our 5G Standalone service and its rapid subscriber uptake, driving premium ARPU uplifts and positioning us for enterprise wins. Our investments in network modernization and fiber expansion are also paying off, driving increased customer satisfaction and loyalty across wireless and broadband. Furthermore, we have focused on content synergies and streaming bundles, which has allowed us to maintain profitability amid cord-cutting trends. Finally, our strategic focus remains on delivering sustainable shareholder returns through disciplined capital allocation and free cash flow generation.

Mike Patel: Thank you, Sarah. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $22.4 billion, representing a 5% increase year-over-year. Our adjusted EBITDA was $6.8 billion, with a margin of 30.4%. We continue to manage our expenses effectively and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year. Our capital expenditures were $4.8 billion, primarily driven by investments in our 5G network expansion.

As we dive deeper into our forward-looking guidance, I'd like to focus on our capital expenditure plans for network investments, which remain the cornerstone of our growth strategy in this dynamic telecom and media landscape. For the full year 2024, we are guiding capex for network investments to a range of $18.5 billion to $20.0 billion, representing about 18-20% of our projected revenue and a modest 3% increase at the midpoint from our 2023 actuals of $19.2 billion. This guidance reflects our disciplined approach to balancing aggressive network modernization with strong free cash flow generation, targeting over $12 billion in FCF for the year.

Let me break this down by key investment categories, as transparency here is critical for modeling our trajectory. First, wireless network investments, which will account for approximately 55% or $10.2 to $11.0 billion of our total network capex. We're accelerating our 5G Standalone core deployment, now live in 85% of our top 100 markets, up from 65% a year ago. This includes $4.5 billion earmarked for C-band and mmWave spectrum utilization—leveraging our $3.2 billion auction win from FCC Auction 110 last year—to deliver gigabit speeds and ultra-low latency for enterprise 5G private networks. We're also investing $2.8 billion in Open RAN initiatives, partnering with Nokia and Samsung, which has already reduced our RAN capex intensity by 15% per site compared to proprietary gear. Trends here are clear: 5G subscriber penetration hit 62% in Q2, driving a 4% YoY ARPU uplift from premium plans, and we're forecasting mid-teens growth in 5G fixed wireless access broadband, targeting 2 million new households by year-end to compete head-on with T-Mobile's aggressive FWA push.

Wireline and fiber investments come in at 30% or $5.6 to $6.0 billion, with a heavy emphasis on FTTH expansion. We've passed 45 million locations with fiber, up 20% YoY, and plan to add another 5 million in 2024, focusing on underserved suburban and rural markets in the Midwest and Southeast U.S. This includes $1.2 billion for next-gen PON upgrades like XGSPON and 25G PON to support 10G symmetrical speeds, aligning with the Biden administration's BEAD program where we've secured $1.8 billion in preliminary grants. Regionally, U.S. wireline capex density remains high at $450 per passed home, but we're seeing payback periods shorten to under 4 years thanks to 35% take rates and bundling with our Nexus Stream media service, which now boasts 18 million SVOD subs.

The remaining 15% or $2.7 to $3.0 billion goes to media and edge infrastructure, critical for our converged telecom-media model. This funds CDN expansions with Akamai and our own edge nodes—$1.1 billion—to handle the surge in 8K streaming and cloud gaming, where latency under 10ms is table stakes. We're also deploying $800 million in AI-optimized content orchestration for our Nexus Stream platform, integrating with hyperscalers like AWS Outposts to personalize recommendations and reduce churn by 2-3 points. In Europe, where we operate via our joint venture with Vodafone in Germany and the UK, media capex is ramped up 25% YoY to counter DAZN and Sky's sports streaming dominance, supporting our 4K HDR UEFA Champions League carriage.

Strategically, this capex envelope positions us for sustainable mid-single-digit revenue growth through 2026. We're shifting from peak 5G buildout—where capex peaked at 22% of revenue in 2022—to optimization, with small cell densification now comprising 40% of wireless spend versus 25% last year. ROI metrics are solid: our 5G IRR exceeds 25%, and fiber NPV per node is $8,500. Risks include supply chain delays in semiconductors, which we've mitigated with dual-sourcing from TSMC and Intel, and potential spectrum renewal costs post-2028. Internationally, in Latin America via our Claro partnership, we're throttling capex to $1.2 billion flat due to FX headwinds in Brazil and Argentina, prioritizing EBITDA margins over volume.

Looking ahead, we expect network capex as a percentage of revenue to trend down to 16-18% by 2025 as deployments mature and spectrum assets are fully lit. This will unlock dividend growth and $5 billion in share repurchases next year.

Before moving on, let me highlight our operating expense management initiatives and their direct impact on profitability. In the hyper-competitive telecom and media landscape—amidst ongoing cord-cutting pressures, the streaming wars with players like Netflix and Disney+, and the capex-intensive 5G and fiber deployments—we've been laser-focused on OpEx discipline without compromising our network quality or customer experience.

Total operating expenses for Q2 came in at $2.85 billion, down 8.2% year-over-year, or approximately $255 million below our prior-year quarter. This represents the strongest quarterly OpEx reduction we've delivered in the past three years, driving adjusted EBITDA to $1.75 billion—a 15% YoY increase—and expanding our EBITDA margin from 28.4% to 32.1%. On a full-year basis through Q2, we've realized cumulative OpEx savings of $725 million, putting us on track to exceed our $900 million full-year target. These savings flowed straight through to the bottom line, boosting diluted EPS by $0.28, or 12%, excluding one-time items.

Our biggest lever continues to be in network operations optimization, delivering $180 million in savings, or 62% of total. We've shifted from heavy capex burn—think our $12 billion 5G Standalone core rollout last year—to smarter, opex-light efficiencies. We've implemented AI-driven predictive maintenance across our 250,000 tower sites and edge data centers, partnering with Ericsson and Nokia for machine learning models that reduced unplanned outages by 22% and field technician dispatches by 35%. This alone saved $95 million in labor and transport costs.

Regionally, in North America—our core market with 85 million wireless subs—we virtualized 40% of our radio access network footprint, cutting energy costs by 18% amid rising power prices. In Europe, where regulatory pressures from the EU's Green Deal are intensifying, we renegotiated tower leases with American Tower and our JV partner Vantage Towers, achieving a 12% blended rate reduction on $450 million in annual leases. And in APAC, our India joint venture with Reliance Jio leveraged shared spectrum and small-cell densification to trim backhaul expenses by 25%, or $40 million. The result? Network OpEx as a percentage of revenue dropped from 22% to 19%, directly supporting our ARPU stability at $48.50 despite competitive pricing from T-Mobile and Verizon.

In content and programming cost discipline, we achieved $85 million in savings, or 30% of total. In media, where content rights eat up 45% of our segment OpEx, we've been aggressive. With linear TV viewership down 15% YoY per Nielsen data, we restructured deals for our 50-channel portfolio, including bundling with our Hulu-like streaming service, Nexus Stream. We exited underperforming sports rights—like regional NHL packages—for $35 million in annual savings and shifted to targeted FAST channels, boosting ad revenue offsets by 8%.

Strategically, we're countering the Netflix/Disney pricing power by co-producing originals with Lionsgate and AMC, reducing acquisition costs by 20% on $300 million in spend. In EMEA, GDPR compliance and local content quotas forced a pivot, but we localized 30% of our library via AI dubbing tools from Synthesia, saving $15 million versus traditional localization. This initiative not only cut costs but improved churn by 2.5 points in our 25 million streaming subs.

Back-office streamlining rounded out the wins with corporate and SG&A efficiencies of $65 million in savings, or 23% of total, with some overlap. We completed Phase 2 of our SAP S/4HANA ERP migration, automating 70% of procurement and invoicing workflows, which slashed SG&A by 11%. Workforce optimization—through attrition and upskilling rather than layoffs—reduced headcount by 4,200 FTEs, or 7%, saving $50 million in comp. Our zero-based budgeting process, now enterprise-wide, scrutinized every line item, yielding $20 million from vendor consolidation, like merging AWS and Azure cloud contracts.

Regionally, in Latin America—where currency volatility hit us last year—we hedged $200 million in local OpEx exposures, stabilizing costs despite 10% inflation in Brazil. These aren't one-offs; they're embedded in our 'Efficient Growth' framework, benchmarking against peers like AT&T's post-Warner spin efficiencies and Comcast's Peacock synergies. We've decoupled OpEx growth from revenue—now running at 1:1 versus historical 1.2:1—positioning us for 500bps of margin expansion by FY25. Risks like supply chain disruptions for subsea cables or FCC spectrum auctions are mitigated via $500 million in multi-year hedges.

Looking ahead, Q3 OpEx guidance is $2.82-$2.88 billion, implying another $200 million+ in savings. This fuels our $0.85 dividend hike and $3 billion buyback authorization. We're proving that in telecom/media, disciplined OpEx isn't just cost-cutting—it's a profitability engine.

I'll now turn to our content and media segment, which continues to be a cornerstone of our diversified portfolio. This segment encompasses our direct-to-consumer streaming platforms—Nexus Stream, our flagship SVOD service—along with linear TV bundles, FAST channels via Nexus Free, content licensing to third parties, and digital advertising across our owned and operated properties. In an industry navigating cord-cutting pressures, the streaming wars, and the shift toward hybrid AVOD-SVOD models, we're executing strategically to drive broadband attachment and ARPU expansion through bundling with our core telecom services.

Content and media segment revenue came in at $2.75 billion for Q2, up 12% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter. This marks our strongest quarterly growth in three years, outpacing the broader U.S. pay-TV market, which contracted 4% per Nielsen data. Subscription revenue, which accounts for 62% of segment total or $1.71 billion, grew 15% YoY, driven by net subscriber additions and ARPU uplift. Our ad-supported tier, launched last year in partnership with our ad tech stack inspired by The Trade Desk integrations, now represents 28% of our base and contributed an incremental $120 million.

Advertising revenue surged 22% to $750 million, fueled by an 18% increase in impression volume from FAST inventory and premium sports programming. CPMs rose 5% to $28, benefiting from targeted addressable TV ads leveraging our 5G-enabled edge computing for real-time personalization—similar to what Roku and Disney have pioneered. Content licensing and other added $290 million, up 6% YoY, with strong renewals from international operators like Sky in Europe and Jio in India, where we're syndicating our original unscripted series.

Profitability remains robust. Adjusted EBITDA for the segment reached $925 million, delivering a 33.6% margin—expansion of 210 basis points YoY. This reflects disciplined content spend at 45% of revenue, down from 48% last year, thanks to our data-driven greenlighting process using AI models akin to Netflix's for churn prediction and content ROI forecasting. Operating expenses grew only 7% YoY, moderated by synergies from our recent merger with StreamCo, which unlocked $150 million in annual cost savings through unified CDN infrastructure on AWS and Akamai.

Turning to subscriber metrics, we ended Q2 with 48.2 million global subscription RGUs across Nexus Stream and our bundled linear-streaming packs—a net addition of 1.8 million sequentially and 4.2 million YoY. Churn improved to 1.2% monthly, our lowest in two years, versus the industry average of 1.8% per Antenna data, due to enhanced retention tactics like personalized bundles tied to our fiber broadband.

Domestic U.S. subscribers hit 32.5 million, +1.1 million net adds. ARPU reached $16.80, up 4% YoY, propelled by 65% broadband attachment rates—our "StreamFi" bundle, which pairs unlimited 5G data with ad-free streaming, now drives 40% of new adds. This mirrors Comcast's Xfinity Stream success but with deeper 5G integration for 4K/HDR low-latency sports. International reached 15.7 million RGUs, +700k net adds, representing 35% YoY growth. APAC led with 9.2 million subs (+1.2 million adds), where Nexus Stream Hindi and our JV with Reliance Jio captured share in the $10B Indian OTT market amid JioCinema's post-IPL surge. EMEA added 400k to reach 4.8 million, bolstered by UEFA Champions League rights and a Sky Deutschland carriage deal. LatAm lagged at +100k adds to 1.7 million, pressured by economic headwinds and Vivo/Claro competition, but ARPU there rose 7% to $9.50 on premium sports upsells.

Blended ARPU stood at $15.40, up 3.5% YoY, with contributions from price increases implemented Q1 across 70% of base, add-on tiers like 4K Max ($3/month), and affiliate revenue sharing from our 25 million linear MVPD subs, down 2% YoY but stabilized via vMVPD pivots like our Fubo partnership.

We're bucking the cord-cutting tide—U.S. pay-TV households fell another 1.5 million per MoffettNathanson, yet our total video ecosystem grew 8%. FAST viewership hours jumped 35% to 2.1 billion, with channels like "Nexus Sports Free" averaging 500k MAUs, capitalizing on Tubi/Pluto TV momentum. However, content costs remain elevated post-strikes, with amortized spend up 10% to $1.24 billion, though offset by hits like our "Global Games" esports league, which boosted Q2 engagement 25%.

Technical initiatives include our $500 million investment in a next-gen CDN with 5G slicing for sub-1-second latency—live in 40 U.S. markets and rolling out to 100 by year-end. We've also deployed ML-powered recommendation engines, lifting session depth 18% and reducing churn by 15%, on par with YouTube's algorithms. On the ad front, our CTV SSP now integrates with Magnite and PubMatic, enabling 30% more fill rates.

North America, 75% of revenue, shows resilient growth amid Netflix/Disney+ price hikes; our sports-heavy slate, including NFL Sunday Ticket carriage and NBA rights renewal, captured 12% share of U.S. streaming sports hours per Samba TV. APAC, 15%, sees hyper-growth from mobile-first markets; Indonesia and Philippines pilots of 5G multicast streaming yielded 25% higher engagement. EMEA/LatAm, 10%, focuses on selective expansion, targeting 35% EBITDA margins by FY25.

Looking ahead, we're positioning Nexus as the "telecom-streaming super app." Key moves include a $2B FY24 original content commitment with 20 new series/greenlights, emphasizing IP like "EchoVerse," a sci-fi franchise rivaling Amazon's Rings of Power; 80% attach rate goal for StreamFi by EOY, leveraging our 60 million broadband subs; eyeing tuck-ins in FAST and ad tech post-StreamCo; renewed Disney bundle talks could add 2-3 million subs. Guidance: Q3 revenue $2.8-2.9B (11-14% YoY), EBITDA margin 34%, with 1.5-2.0M net adds. FY24 full-year: $11.2B revenue (+13%), 34% margins. This segment's momentum underscores our "Connect & Entertain" thesis—fusing telecom pipes with premium content for sticky, high-margin growth.

As we wrap up, I'd like to turn to one of our top priorities: delivering sustainable, attractive returns to shareholders through a balanced capital allocation framework. In the telecom and media sectors, where capex-intensive network investments meet the high-growth demands of 5G, fiber broadband, and streaming content, maintaining dividend sustainability requires disciplined free cash flow generation, prudent leverage management, and strategic revenue diversification.

Our dividend remains a cornerstone. We currently pay a quarterly dividend of $0.55 per share, equating to an annualized $2.20 per share. At yesterday's close, this delivers a forward yield of 4.8%, well above the S&P 500 Telecom Select Industry Index average of 3.2% and competitive with media peers like Comcast at 3.1% or Verizon at 6.5%. We've grown this dividend at a 6% CAGR over the past five years—from $1.65 in 2019—supported by consistent EPS expansion and FCF outperformance. Year-to-date through Q2 2024, we've distributed $1.10 per share, or approximately $1.8 billion in total dividends based on our average diluted shares outstanding of 1.65 billion.

Our metrics show robust coverage. Our trailing 12-month payout ratio stands at 52% of adjusted EPS of $4.23, down from 58% a year ago, reflecting 12% EPS growth driven by wireless service revenue up 5% and media ad sales surging 15% on targeted programmatic platforms. More critically, the FCF payout ratio is a healthy 42%, with TTM FCF of $5.2 billion easily covering the $2.2 billion annualized dividend 2.4x. Q2 alone generated $1.4 billion, up 18% YoY, from adjusted EBITDA of $4.1 billion (margin 48%, +200bps YoY) minus normalized capex of $2.3 billion (17% of revenue, trending toward 16% in 2025 as 5G SA rollout matures). Post-dividend, working capital, and minor M&A tuck-ins, we ended Q2 with $1.1 billion in levered FCF, fueling our returns program.

Leverage provides resilience. Our net debt to adjusted EBITDA ratio is 2.6x, down from 2.9x at year-end 2023 and comfortably below our 3.0x-3.5x target band—similar to AT&T's 2.8x or T-Mobile's 2.4x post-merger. This deleveraging stems from $1.2 billion in debt paydowns YTD and $800 million from asset monetizations, including tower sales mirroring Crown Castle deals. Interest coverage is 8.5x, insulating us from Fed rate volatility, with 85% of debt fixed at an average cost of 3.8%.

Total shareholder returns YTD: $3.7 billion, blending dividends and share repurchases. Our $4 billion open-market buyback authorization, announced post our 2023 spectrum auction wins, is 72% complete—we repurchased 45 million shares at an average of $48, retiring 2.7% of float and yielding $2.2 billion deployed. This opportunistic program targets 4-6% annual reduction in shares outstanding, accretive to EPS at current multiples. Combined, our total shareholder yield YTD is 7.9% (4.8% dividend + 3.1% buyback), outpacing the Telecom/Media sector median of 5.4% per FactSet data. Over the past three years, cumulative returns total $12.4 billion, delivering a 12% annualized TSR versus the S&P 500's 10%.

Regionally, in North America (82% of revenue), postpaid mobile ARPU grew 4% to $52/month on 5G premium plans, with 65% of our 120 million subs on midband 5G—mirroring T-Mobile's playbook but with higher fixed-line bundling (75% penetration, adding $15/month household revenue). FCF here covers 110% of regional dividends. Europe (12% of revenue) faces regulatory scrutiny on wholesale pricing, yet converged fiber-mobile bundles drove 8% broadband net adds (1.2 million), with FTTH passings hitting 45% coverage versus Vodafone's 40%. EBITDA margins expanded 150bps to 46% via network sharing with Orange, bolstering FCF. In APAC/JVs (6%), high data usage in India (via our Airtel stake) yielded 22% EBITDA growth, though capex for 5G sub-6GHz offsets some returns—still, JV dividends to us hit $450 million YTD.

We affirm confidence in dividend sustainability through 2027+. We expect 2024 FCF of $5.5-$5.7 billion (midpoint +8% YoY), supporting a 5-7% dividend hike in Q1 2025 to ~$2.32/share. This assumes capex at $9.0-$9.5 billion (down from $10.2 billion in 2023 as Open RAN trials in 15% of new sites cut opex 20%), offset by 4% service revenue growth from enterprise 5G private networks and media streaming subs up 12% on our platform, now at 28 million paid users with 92% retention via AI personalization.

Key initiatives include capex efficiency with $1.5 billion in savings over 2024-2026 from virtualized RAN and disaggregated architectures, targeting 15% ROI on fiber investments (vs. 12% industry avg per Dell'Oro). Our 30 million FTTH homes passed yield 85% take rates, rivaling Verizon Fios. Cost synergies of $900 million run-rate from our 2023 media ops consolidation, with opex-to-revenue falling to 38%. Revenue accelerants like $2 billion in new 3.5GHz C-band spectrum (won at 2024 FCC auction for $1.8 billion, 40% below reserve) enabling FWA to capture 2 million underserved broadband households. Media-side, carriage fee hikes with MVPDs and FAST channel expansions (500+ titles) counter Netflix/Disney+ churn. M&A discipline with $1.5 billion tuck-in pipeline for regional fiber assets, funded 50/50 debt/FCF, maintaining leverage <3x.

In summary, our dividend is not just sustainable—it's growing, backed by FCF coverage >2x, low leverage, and a total returns framework delivering $3.7 billion YTD with more to come. This positions Nexus Telecom as a sector standout for income investors amid 5G maturation and streaming consolidation.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, press star one on your telephone keypad. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the capex guidance for network investments, particularly how you're balancing wireless and fiber spends with FCF targets?

Mike Patel: Certainly, John. As I detailed earlier, our $18.5 to $20 billion full-year network capex guide prioritizes wireless at 55%, with $10.2 to $11 billion fueling 5G SA acceleration to 85% coverage in top markets and Open RAN for 15% lower intensity. Fiber gets $5.6 to $6 billion for 5 million more passes, leveraging BEAD grants, while media/edge takes the rest for CDN and AI personalization. This supports over $12 billion FCF, with capex/revenue dipping to 16-18% by 2025, unlocking repurchases and dividend growth. Risks like supply chains are hedged, and Latin America capex is flat at $1.2 billion for margin focus.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Johnson: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Could you elaborate on your plans for the content and media segment, especially subscriber growth and margin expansion amid competition?

Sarah Chen: Thanks, Emily. Mike covered the strong Q2 results—$2.75 billion revenue up 12%, $925 million EBITDA at 33.6% margin, 48.2 million RGUs with 1.8 million adds. U.S. at 32.5 million drives 65% broadband attach via StreamFi, APAC surges to 9.2 million on Jio JV. Churn at 1.2% from AI recs and bundles. Ahead, Q3 guides $2.8-2.9 billion revenue, 34% margins, 1.5-2 million adds; FY24 $11.2 billion up 13%. We're bundling deeper, investing $2 billion in originals like EchoVerse, expanding FAST, and eyeing Disney partnerships for more subs, fusing pipes and content for high-margin growth.

Alex Rivera: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Sarah, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Sarah Chen: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
